Committing the files, registering four sol seats, and sending the nine jobs.No cancel route exists, and duplicating the queued jobs would either waste quota or put two seats on one file. I'll leave this round as it is and record the slip.The first round is running: nine lemma jobs across five problems, on four new Codex seats (`lemma-1` to `lemma-4`, gpt-5.6-sol). They work in their own worktree, `~/worktrees/apm-lean/lemmas` on branch `lemmas`, so the canonical tree and the topology loops aren't affected. **Setup:** - **One file per lemma.** Each lemma has its own copy of its problem's blueprint, in `holes/labs/lemmas/

/.lean`. The lemma sits between `BEGIN/END SEAT AREA` markers, and seats may only edit inside them. - **A mechanical checker.** `~/notes/packets/lemmas/lemmatool.py check P NAME` rejects a result unless: - everything outside the markers is byte-identical; - the lemma's statement is unchanged; - there's no `sorry`, `admit` or `axiom` in the edited part; - the file compiles; - `#print axioms` for the lemma shows no `sorryAx`. So I'm not relying on the seats' own reports. It already refuses the untouched files. The compile and axiom check hasn't run yet; the first returned job will exercise it. - **Landing a result.** A passing lemma gets spliced into the blueprint and committed. When all of a problem's lemmas pass, its `Main.lean` becomes the complete proof, and the registry check confirms the statement didn't move. - **The instructions** say to prove missing Mathlib facts rather than stop, and to leave a compiling partial with the exact remaining goal if time runs out. The m99A02 job gets the lines-avoiding-the-origin route, plus a warning that it can't use the other m99A02 lemma. **One mistake on my part:** I assigned seats by problem, so each problem's two lemmas run one after the other on the same seat. This round is therefore four problems in parallel, not lemmas within a problem. There's no way to cancel queued jobs, and re-sending them would either waste quota or put two seats on the same file, so I've left it.
